memory_verse.label: Bible Reference
memory_verse.text: "and do not show favoritism to a poor person in a lawsuit." - Exodus 23:3 (NIV)

devotion.label: Devotion
devotion.text:
This is a surprising command. We might expect God, who so fiercely defends the poor, to say, "Always rule in favour of the poor man." Instead He says the opposite: do not show favouritism even to the poor. Justice must be blind. A person's poverty does not automatically make them right, just as their wealth does not automatically make them right. Truth is truth, regardless of who is rich or poor.

This reveals the beautiful evenness of God's justice. He defends the poor from being oppressed, yes — but He does not want justice bent in anyone's favour, not even out of misplaced sympathy. To twist the truth to favour the poor would still be to twist the truth. And a justice that can be bent in one direction can always be bent in the other. God wants a fairness that treats every person by the same honest standard.

There is a lesson here for our own hearts. It is easy to let our sympathies or our biases decide what we believe to be true, favouring the people we like or pity and dismissing those we do not. But God calls us to a deeper honesty — to seek what is actually true and right, not merely what feels comfortable or kind in the moment. Real love and real justice always walk hand in hand with truth.

reflection.label: Reflection
reflection.text:
Do I let my sympathies or biases bend my judgment of what is true?
How can I pursue fairness that treats every person by the same honest standard?

prayer.label: Prayer
prayer.text: Father, You are perfectly just and show no partiality. Free me from biased judgments, and help me pursue truth and fairness for every person, whoever they are. Amen.
